concepts.def: Travel abroad vocabulary: el extranjero (abroad), el pasaporte, la aduana (customs), el vuelo (flight), reservar (to book).
Accommodation phrases: una habitación doble, con vistas al mar (sea view), la recepción, '¿Tiene habitaciones libres?'
At the station: un billete de ida y vuelta (return ticket), el andén (platform), 'El tren llega con retraso' (the train is delayed).
Global issues vocabulary: la pobreza (poverty), el cambio climático, la guerra (war), los refugiados, la ayuda humanitaria.
Nationalities agree and are lowercase: francés/francesa, inglés/inglesa, español/española: 'Ella es francesa'.
Narrate past trips with the preterite: 'El año pasado fui a México, visité las pirámides y lo pasé fenomenal'.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Area E: The International World — a core area of GCSE Spanish.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area E: The International World brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area E: The International World.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: 'Un billete de ida y vuelta' is what kind of ticket?
options: A return ticket
A single ticket
A bus pass
A lottery ticket

mcqs.q: In 'Fui a México el verano pasado', which tense is 'fui'?
options: The preterite, for a completed past action
The present tense
The future tense
The conditional
Climate change
A change of clothes
Currency exchange
A weather forecast

mcqs.q: Which sentence uses the nationality correctly?
options: Ella es francesa
Ella es francés
Ella es Francesa de
Ella está Francia
Fui is the future tense of tener.
It can come from both ir (to go) and ser (to be); context tells you which - 'Fui a España' means 'I went to Spain'.
Fui only ever comes from ser, so 'Fui a España' must mean 'I was Spain'.
Nationalities are always written entirely in capitals.

mcqs.q: Should nationalities be capitalised in Spanish as in English?
options: No - Spanish writes nationalities and languages in lowercase: 'Es francesa y habla inglés'.
Nationalities take a capital letter, as in English.
Slow.
Nationalities are always written entirely in capitals.
Long - 'un viaje largo' is a long journey.
Slow.
Fui is the future tense of tener.
Large or big, because of the spelling.
